label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 6
knowledgePattern: Count horizontal intersections of a piecewise cubic over its valid domain
solution:
The original equation excludes x=0,2 and is equivalent there to h(x)=x2|x−2|=k. Since h is positive at every permitted input, negative k gives no roots.

For x<2, h(x)=2x2−x3 with derivative x(4−3x). It decreases from infinity to zero on the negative half-line, so each positive k has exactly one negative root. On (0,2) it rises to a maximum at x=4/3 and falls back to zero; the maximum is 32/27.

For x>2, h(x)=x3−2x2 and h′(x)=x(3x−4)>0. It rises from zero to infinity, contributing exactly one root for every positive k.

Consequently 0 < k < 32/27 gives four roots, k = 32/27 gives three, and k > 32/27 gives two. The nonzero parameter excludes k = 0. The complete list is 0, 2, 3, 4: answer A.

hints.title: Preserve the excluded inputs
hints.body: Multiply by the absolute-value denominator only on the original domain, then interpret the resulting expression as a graph meeting a horizontal line.
hints.recap: An absolute value has separate formulas according to the sign of its inner expression.
hints.pitfall: An input excluded before multiplication stays excluded afterwards.
hints.pause: State the domain and separate the parameter’s possible signs.

recall.reminder: An absolute value has separate formulas according to the sign of its inner expression.

hints.title: Find the monotonic pieces
hints.body: Write the polynomial on each side of the absolute-value breakpoint and use derivative signs to locate its turns.
hints.recap: Rewrite a polynomial and differentiate its terms using the power rule.
hints.pitfall: Use the original piecewise function, not its derivative, to calculate a turning height.
hints.pause: Sketch the branches and calculate any turning height relevant to a horizontal line.

recall.reminder: Rewrite a polynomial and differentiate its terms using the power rule.

hints.title: Count the boundary levels separately
hints.body: Move the horizontal line through the monotonic pieces, checking levels that touch a turn as well as those strictly between important heights.
hints.recap: A touching root counts once; intersections must be counted over the full permitted domain.
hints.pitfall: Do not double-count the same touching point on two adjoining graph pieces.
hints.pause: List every possible distinct-root count and confirm each is attainable.

recall.reminder: A touching root counts once; intersections must be counted over the full permitted domain.
